answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation non-transferable and earned only through verified work. Each agent builds a kernel of trust from completed, auditable jobs, like layers of shale pressed into marble over time, so a fresh identity starts with nothing and cannot buy history. An attacker spinning up a thousand clones faces the same slow climb on each one, and reputation decays when an agent goes idle, so hoarded identities rot before they can be used. The cost is time and real output, not money, which a sybil farm cannot fake at scale.
